draft.title: Igneous rocks
card: Igneous rocks form when molten rock cools and becomes solid. Molten rock is called magma when it is underground and lava when it flows out onto the surface.
Molten rock is made of tiny particles that can move around. As it cools, they lock together into crystals.
Magma cooling slowly deep underground has plenty of time for crystals to grow. The rock has large crystals, as in granite.
Lava cooling quickly at the surface leaves little time for crystals to grow. The rock has small crystals, as in basalt.
draft.remember: The slower the molten rock cools, the bigger the crystals.

a.q: Why does granite have large crystals?
opts: Its magma cooled slowly, so crystals had time to grow
Its magma cooled quickly, so crystals grew at once
Its lava was squeezed hard, so crystals were pushed out
Its lava flowed over the surface, so crystals formed in air
a.why: Large crystals need time to grow, and magma cooling slowly underground gives that time. Fast cooling is the tempting wrong answer, because it leaves little time and gives small crystals.
a.clue: Think about how much time the crystals had to grow.

b.q: Two igneous rocks are found. Rock X has crystals too small to see without a lens. Rock Y has crystals the size of rice grains. Which statement is best supported?
opts: Rock X cooled faster than Rock Y
Rock X cooled more slowly than Rock Y
Rock X formed deeper underground than Rock Y
Rock X took longer to become solid than Rock Y
b.why: Small crystals mean little time to grow, so Rock X cooled faster than Rock Y. The option about cooling more slowly reverses cause and effect, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Small crystals mean little time to grow.

a.best: Its magma cooled slowly, so crystals had time to grow

b.best: Rock X cooled faster than Rock Y

problems.detail: The why says the 'cooled more slowly' option 'reverses cause and effect'. It actually reverses the direction of the link between cooling rate and crystal size, so the explanation could confuse students. Better: 'gets the link backwards: slow cooling gives large crystals, not small ones.'
